Maybe he was busy with something urgent or his phone died. What are some things that might make you think this thought isn't entirely true?

That's a good point to consider!  Based on your thought, it could be that you're mind reading Bill's intentions – assuming he doesn't care because he didn't answer – without knowing for sure what was going on. It could also be all-or-nothing thinking, where if he didn't pick up, you automatically assume no one cares about you at all. Do either of those thoughts resonate with your experience?
I think I made the "mind reading" mistake.

Maybe he was busy on something that he can't pick up the phone. Maybe tomorrow I find him in person.
That's a great shift in thinking! It sounds much more balanced. How intense is that feeling of frustration now compared to when you first thought no one cared?

It sounds like you were feeling really down after Bill didn't answer your calls. It's understandable to feel hurt when someone doesn't respond, but it’s important to remember that there could be many reasons why he didn't pick up. You even mentioned his past reassurance that he'd help if you needed him!  

By exploring the evidence and challenging those automatic thoughts, you were able to shift towards a more balanced perspective.  That takes real strength and insight. Remember, sometimes reaching out in person can be helpful too.
